topic: Lambda Capture Dangling Risk: By-Reference and `this`
explanation: Default capture modes introduce two primary risks related to lifetime: 1. Default by-reference capture (`[&]`) captures local stack variables. If the lambda outlives the scope of creation (e.g., stored in a global container or returned), the captured references become dangling. 2. Default by-value capture (`[=]`) implicitly captures the `this` pointer by value if a member variable is used. If the object pointed to by `this` is destroyed before the lambda is invoked, the captured `this` pointer becomes dangling, leading to undefined behavior upon invocation.
practical_example: An asynchronous scheduler takes a lambda captured with `[=]`. The lambda uses a member variable. If the host object is destroyed immediately after scheduling the task, the lambda will execute later, dereferencing a stale `this` pointer.
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
